title: Determination of the appropriate tracheal tube size in children and adults with short stature due to skeletal dysplasia
summary:
Many people with short stature due to skeletal dysplasias may undergo surgical procedures at some point in their lives. For certain interventions, the placement of an endotracheal tube is required as part of general anesthesia. While normative values, formulas, and recommendations exist for selecting the optimal tube size in average‑stature children and adults, such guidance is lacking for individuals with short stature. This study aims to contribute to developing a decision aid for selecting an appropriately sized endotracheal tube in people with short stature, thereby improving anesthesia safety for individuals with skeletal dysplasia.
The approximately 15‑minute interview and examination (measurement of the distal phalanges of the 4th and 5th fingers, assessment of common anesthesiologic airway evaluation tests, ultrasound of the trachea) will take place either during the Short Stature Forum 2026 or in the neurosurgical operating area of the University Hospital Mannheim. No additional clinic visits or follow‑up examinations are required.
